reason: Section 48.4 includes definitions, ongoing validity of ground staked claims, priority against map staked claims, and conversion timing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ground staked and map staked mineral claim definitions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 48.4(1) defines ground staked mineral claim and map staked mineral claim.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of ground staked mineral claim and map staked mineral claim.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Validity and renewal of ground staked mineral claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.4(2) through 48.4(4) preserve validity and renewal of ground staked mineral claims until expiry, surrender, cancellation, or conversion.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how ground staked mineral claims remain valid and are renewed before conversion.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Priority and map staked claim limits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.4(5) through 48.4(7) address priority over later map staked claims and limits on registering map staked claims over covered land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how ground staked claims affect priority and registration of map staked claims.

reason: Section 48.5 extends another ground staked claim over the whole mineral claim unit when a partial ground staked claim expires, is surrendered, or is cancelled.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Extension over claim unit after ground staked claim ends

evidenceText: Extension of title over mineral claim unit on expiry or surrender of ground staked mineral claims

proposedGroups.reason: Section 48.5 extends another ground staked claim over the whole mineral claim unit when a partial ground staked claim expires, is surrendered, or is cancelled.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when title over a mineral claim unit is extended after a ground staked mineral claim ends.

reason: Section 48.6 confirms and ratifies certain approved agreements and deems related claims to be map staked mineral claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ratified agreements and deemed map staked claims
proposedGroups.reason: Section 48.6 confirms and ratifies certain approved agreements and deems related claims to be map staked mineral claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how certain subsection 25(2) agreements and related claims are validated and characterized.

reason: Section 48.7 has distinct steps for voluntary conversion of ground staked mineral claims: application, Recorder determination, holder election, registration, and effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application for voluntary conversion
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.7(1) and 48.7(2) identify who may apply and require written application before expiry.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may apply to convert ground staked mineral claims and when the application must be made.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder determination and holder election
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.7(3) and 48.7(4) require the Recorder to determine claim units, claim area, and conversion information and require the holder to elect conversion.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Recorder determines and how the holder elects voluntary conversion.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration date and continuation effect of converted claim
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.7(5) through 48.7(8) address registration, date, and deemed continuation after conversion.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the registration, date, and continuation effect of voluntary conversion to a map staked mineral claim.

reason: Section 48.8 has distinct mandatory conversion topics for the Recorder's duty, determinations, registration, priority, continuation, conflicts, and rights.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder duty to convert ground staked claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 48.8(1) requires the Recorder to convert all ground staked mineral claims within 90 days after commencement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Recorder's mandatory conversion duty and deadline.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder determinations for each converted claim
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.8(2) and 48.8(3) require determinations of claim units, claim area, and other information, and allow use of available information.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Recorder determines for mandatory conversion.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration date and continuation effects
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.8(4) through 48.8(7) address registration, date, and deemed continuation of converted claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the registration, date, and continuation effects of mandatory conversion.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Conflicts errors and rights after conversion
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 48.8(8) through 48.8(10) address conflicts, errors, omissions, and preserved rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how conflicts, errors, omissions, and rights are handled after mandatory conversion.

reason: The target contains only a repeal notation for section 49.
Section 50 deems a mineral claim properly registered if section 44 was complied with and no notice of dispute is filed within 60 days, absent fraud.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Deemed proper registration absent timely dispute or fraud
proposedGroups.reason: Section 50 deems a mineral claim properly registered if section 44 was complied with and no notice of dispute is filed within 60 days, absent fraud.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a mineral claim is deemed properly registered and protected from dispute or cancellation.

reason: Section 51 bases mineral claim priority on the date and time of confirmation of registration recorded by the registry.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Priority of mineral claims by confirmation time
proposedGroups.reason: Section 51 bases mineral claim priority on the date and time of confirmation of registration recorded by the registry.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how mineral claim priority is determined.

reason: Section 52 separates notice and order for non-compliance, cancellation, appeal, and land withdrawal effects.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder notice and order for non-compliance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 52(1) allows the Recorder to notify a holder of non-compliance and order compliance within a specified period.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Recorder's notice and compliance order powers for mineral claim non-compliance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Cancellation and appeal
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 52(2) and 52(3) address cancellation if the holder does not comply and appeal from cancellation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Recorder may cancel a mineral claim for non-compliance and how cancellation may be appealed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Withdrawal of cancelled claim area
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 52(4) withdraws the cancelled claim area from prospecting and registration for the specified period.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the effect of cancellation on the claim area.

reason: Section 53 gives mineral claim holders access and exclusive prospecting, mining, and sampling rights, while imposing liability for actual damage and interference.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mineral claim holder rights and liability
proposedGroups.reason: Section 53 gives mineral claim holders access and exclusive prospecting, mining, and sampling rights, while imposing liability for actual damage and interference.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the rights and liabilities that registration gives a mineral claim holder.

reason: Section 54 states that a mineral claim expires at midnight on the anniversary of registration, subject to renewal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mineral claim expiry at anniversary midnight
proposedGroups.reason: Section 54 states that a mineral claim expires at midnight on the anniversary of registration, subject to renewal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a mineral claim expires.

reason: Section 55 gives holders the right to renew for one, two, or three one-year terms, effective on expiry, and states expiry dates for renewed claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Renewal terms and expiry of renewed mineral claims
proposedGroups.reason: Section 55 gives holders the right to renew for one, two, or three one-year terms, effective on expiry, and states expiry dates for renewed claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how mineral claim renewals take effect and when renewed claims expire.

reason: Section 56 is a detailed renewal requirement provision covering submissions, required work, excess work, fee treatment, reports, and conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Renewal submissions before and after claim expiry
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 56(1) sets pre-expiry statement and fee submissions and post-renewal report and cost statement submissions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the submissions required to register a mineral claim renewal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required work and dollar value rules
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 56(2) through 56(4) address prescribed required work, dollar value, and proof of performance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how required work and dollar value are handled for mineral claim renewals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Excess work credits and allocation
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 56(5) through 56(7) address crediting and allocating excess dollar value of work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when excess work value may be credited or allocated.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Non-compliance condition for renewal
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 56(10) addresses a condition connected to renewal requirements when compliance is at issue.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the condition in subsection 56(10) for mineral claim renewal requirements.

reason: Section 57 prevents expiry when required reports are timely submitted despite consideration delays and requires notice of performed required work and excess credit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Delay while renewal report is considered
proposedGroups.reason: Section 57 prevents expiry when required reports are timely submitted despite consideration delays and requires notice of performed required work and excess credit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the effect of delay in considering renewal work reports and cost statements.
